glosses: to clue in, to prompt; to suggest; to hint (to give someone an answer to something they either don't know or forgot i.e. on a test)
to prompt; to suggest (to lead someone toward what they should say or do)
to autosuggest, to fill in automatically (of software etc, to automatically show information in a field)

Quick; acting without delay.

examples.text: He was very prompt at getting a new job.

glosses: On time; punctual.

examples.text: Be prompt for your appointment.

examples.text: Tell him, I am prompt / To lay my Crowne at's feete, and there to kneele.

glosses: Front: closest or nearest, in futures trading.

examples.text: When physical crude oil transactions are priced, they are usually marked to the prompt month futures contract. The prompt month futures contract is the next futures contract to settle.
The settlement ratio is determined as follows: i) If the prompt futures price of coal at maturity is less than or equal to the floor price, the ratio will be one.

glosses: A reminder or cue.
A word, phrase or line supplied by a prompter to an actor who has forgotten the script.
A reminder or cue.
A suggestion for inspiration given to an author.

examples.text: To cover any probable difference of price which might arise before the expiration of the prompt, which for this article [tea] is three months.

glosses: A sequence of characters that is displayed to indicate that a computer is ready to receive input.

examples.text: I filled in my name where the prompt appeared on the computer screen but my account wasn't recognized.

glosses: Textual input given to a large language model or image model in order to have it generate a desired output.

examples.text: For instance, using the “instruct” mode, I once gave GPT-3 the prompt: “Write an essay discussing the role of metafiction in the work of Italo Calvino.”

glosses: To lead (someone) toward what they should say or do.

examples.text: I prompted him to get a new job.

glosses: To say (something) in order to help or encourage someone to speak.

examples.text: "How did you solve the issue then?" Jason prompted while staring at Lana.

"What is your name, you?" he demanded. The captured youth tried to pull free again, but was obviously tiring. After a moment he stopped his struggling altogether. "Your name?" Simon prompted, this time in a softer tone.
"Malachias." The youth turned away panting.
‘Be warned, Molly,’ Gideon added harshly. ‘I won't ever let you do or say anything that will hurt Crys. Is that understood?’ he prompted determinedly.

glosses: To show or tell (an actor/person) the words they should be saying, or actions they should be doing.

examples.text: If he forgets his words I will prompt him.

glosses: To initiate; to cause or lead to.

examples.text: At first Renie's chain of thought had been prompted by the unsatisfactory nature of phone contact compared to an actual meeting,[…]

The only sour note on a virtually perfect night for England came from shameful 'monkey' chanting aimed at Ashley Cole and Ashley Young from a section of Bulgaria's fans which later prompted an official complaint from the Football Association to Uefa.

On October 6, 1927, Warner Bros. released The Jazz Singer, the first sound-synched feature film, prompting a technological shift of unprecedented speed and unstoppable force. Within two years, nearly every studio release was a talkie.

glosses: To request (a user) to provide input or do something on a computer.

examples.text: The script prompted him to enter his credit account number.

glosses: To provide textual input in the form of ordinary language to (an artificial intelligence or language model) to have it generate a desired output.

examples.text: I want to prompt this new AI art generator to create an image of a panda riding a bike.

examples.text: Спускаясь с лестницы твёрдыми шагами, он свистал сквозь зубы, а злоба всё подсказывала ему обидные, крепкие, камням подобные слова.
